rationale:
structural: The only text of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.fn` is: "Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation." It is a pointer. It names the function form of the read-node operation and cites the declaration that owns it. It has no MUST, SHOULD or MAY clause of its own. It prescribes no signature, type, field or algorithm.

The prescribed signature, `ValidationContext::read(&self, &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>`, and the fingerprint-recording behavior belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read`. That declaration is assessed against its own text. This subject does not duplicate its obligations.

"Criterion code" means whatever `Criterion` implementations users write, as the definition `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.criterion` describes. Examples are `src/sdk/issues.rs#impl[OpenIssue/Criterion<HabeasDomain>]/fn[execute]`, which does call `cx.read`, and `src/authoring/sdk.rs#impl[Review<'_>/Criterion<HabeasDomain>]/fn[execute]`. This is an open set of user code, not a fixed implementation root. Which API that code calls is a usage convention, and no single item in this project has to carry it out. The text's only concrete effect is that reading through the validation context records the dependency. The cited requirement states that effect, so it is not a separate structural obligation here.

No implementation roots were supplied and none are needed. I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.fn` says only that criterion code uses `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for the read operation. It is a pointer that names the API to use. It states no MUST, MUST NOT or SHOULD behavior of its own, and it has no inputs, outputs, boundaries or failure cases to test.

The behavior of `ValidationContext.read` is its own cited requirement, and I did not reassess it. That requirement has the signature and the fingerprint-recording obligation, which it cites to `read_node.inputs`.

The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]` exercises `read` anyway. It reads empty and large Unicode contents and checks the returned contents. It checks that the recorded `Dependency::Node` carries the fingerprint, that later graph changes don't alter the returned contents, and that a missing node returns an error and records no dependency. No further test evidence is needed for this subject.

```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
pub fn read(&self, node: &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>;
::::{definition} application_domain
:phrase: application domain
:::{cite} requirements.sdk.domain
An *application domain* is the application's graph, node contents, and evidence
storage, made available together for criterion execution. In the SDK, it
implements [`Domain`](../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/domain/trait.Domain.html) to supply
its shared types, node and edge operations, and evidence persistence.
:::{definition} content_snapshot
:phrase: snapshot
A *snapshot* is the contents obtained by one observation, paired with the
{term}`requirements.sdk.graph.observation_fingerprint` of those
same contents. [`Snapshot<T>`](../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/graph/struct.Snapshot.html)
represents that pair.
:::{definition} criterion
:phrase: criterion
A *criterion* is a value describing a test to perform on a
{term}`requirements.sdk.graph.node`.
In the SDK, its type implements
[`Criterion<D>`](../../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/graph/trait.Criterion.html) for the
{term}`requirements.sdk.application_domain`. Its
members describe the question's answer, identity, review rules, and execution.
:::{definition} node
:phrase: graph node
A *graph node* is a thing identified in the application's graph, such as a

requirement, a function, a test, or an issue. `Domain::NodeData` identifies the same node across runs. For example, a requirement's qualified name can identify it as its text and implementation edges change.
:::{definition} observation_fingerprint
:phrase: fingerprint
A *fingerprint* is a digest together with the scheme identifying how it was
computed, represented by
[`Fingerprint`](../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/graph/struct.Fingerprint.html).
It describes an observation under those rules; it does not identify the node or
say whether a criterion's answer is favorable.
Both the scheme and digest participate in comparisons.
:::{definition} validation_context
:phrase: validation context
A *validation context* gives a {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.criterion`
the tools to decide whether it is satisfied and records which inputs it uses
during a single execution. An agent called by the criterion shares that context.
:::{req} read_node.behavior
The Rust caller receives the node's complete `D::NodeContent` or the domain's read error.
The tool asks the domain to read the supplied node ID, including when an assigned ID first appears in the `read_node` call.
Each page’s `text` contains the next portion of the node’s formatted contents. Formatting follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.rendering`.
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{req} read_node.mcp
Give `read_node` a node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. The result contains the node’s text. If more
text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.
```text
read_node(NodeAddress) -> {text: string, next?: UUID}
// For a source node the result has these additional fields:
{file: string, selector: string, children: {node: NodeId, file: string, selector: string, header?: string}[]}
